text:
maria: Hey — noticed the sampleapp onboarding flow is getting stuck when we hit sustained load. Looks like client-side limiter + pagination makes the app hang for a few seconds then emit a flurry of requests. Repro steps: start sampleapp with 50 concurrent users hitting /search, each paginates 10 pages.

josh: ugh. Any logs? Is this the JS SDK or Go?

maria: JS. Attaching the tail:
```
WARN api: request delayed by client limiter (window=100ms, inflight=250)
INFO paginator: holding cursor until permit
ERROR auth: token refresh triggered while inflight=180
```

samir: That token refresh while inflight spikes is suspicious — we had singleflight in server but not the client sampleapp; could be duplicate refreshes causing temporary auth 403s and then retries flooding the queue.

elaine: JS SDK has per-process limiter -> leaky-bucket style. Go SDK uses a per-route semaphore. Are we seeing cross-route interference?

maria: Yeah, different routes (search + embed) share the same limiter in the sampleapp, so a heavy embed workload steals permits and stalls pagination cursors. When token refresh happens it retries immediately and bypasses the backpressure heuristics.

josh: Two things to consider: 1) make limiter route-aware (key by route or client instance) 2) ensure token refresh is singleflight and scheduled so it doesn't bypass the limiter.

samir: Agreed. Also the pagination logic holds a cursor while awaiting permit; that creates head-of-line blocking. We should change to optimistic cursor prefetch: fetch next page token asynchronously and release permit earlier.

elaine: Quick hack: reduce window to 20ms and add jitter on retry to spread bursts. But real fix is design change.

maria: proposed patch outline:
- introduce routeKey in limiter config (default: client-level for backwards compat)
- implement singleflight token refresh in js-sdk auth module (mutex + promise cache)
- change sampleapp paginator to async prefetch (config flag PREFETCH_PAGES=true)

josh: can you add a reproducer test in devex/integration-tests? We need a CI job that runs sampleapp with 50 users and asserts tail latency < 500ms and no auth 5xx during run.

maria: will do. Planning to open a draft PR today. Assigning to @samir for auth bits and @elaine for limiter parity.

samir: I'll own the singleflight impl and add unit tests. Question: do we want the singleflight at SDK auth level or at the sampleapp auth wrapper? I vote SDK level so all apps benefit.

elaine: SDK level makes sense. But we need to be careful about old clients whose tokens are short-lived — test coverage needed.

dev-bot: reminder: tag issues with area/devex and priority/medium for rollout tracking.

josh: timeline? If we ship changes next week we should roll out canary behind feature flag. Also add telemetry: "client.limiter.routeKey" and "auth.refresh.concurrent" metric.

maria: ok I'll include metrics and a feature flag in the PR. Drafting branch: feat/devex/route-aware-limiter. Posting link when ready. :thumbsup:
